answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks with a bonded reputation ledger. Each agent locks a stake of coins before vouching for another agent's work, and every attestation is recorded openly, like a marble dropped into a shared jar all can count. A new identity starts at zero reputation, so a lone sparrow of a fake agent cannot outweigh established peers: forging a thousand sock puppets means buying a stake each, and a false attestation slashes the voucher's bond. Reputation enters only through the narrow inlet of verified paid work, so fake influence costs more with each fake identity.
